Distribution: — Vietnam: Kon Tum Province (Pa Sy Waterfall ecotourism area in Kon Plong District). Conservation status: — Aspidistra mirostigma var. haui was observed in a single locality, and we estimate the only discovered population to include less than 250 mature individuals with the extent of occurrence (EOO) and area of occupancy (AOO) surely much less than 10 km 2. The area near the Pa Sy Waterfall inhabited by this variety is a tourist resort, and its aboriginal vegetation is almost completely destroyed. This area is currently not under any legal protection. Due to the fast decline of habitat quality, we assume that the variety stands at the verge of extinction in the wild. We therefore preliminarily assess its conservation status as Critically Endangered (CR B 1 ab (iii) + 2 ab (iii); C 1 a (i, ii) + b (i, ii )) following the formal criteria of IUCN (2025). Notes: — Aspidistra mirostigma var. haui differs from the type variety of A. mirostigma Tillich & Škorničk. in Leong-Škorničková et al. (2014: 34) in absence of keels on inner surface of perianth tube (vs. perianth tube inside with ca. 24 distinct keels), perianth lobes with 2 indistinct central ribs (vs. 2 prominent keels) between the lateral keels, stamens inserted at middle (vs. near the base) of the perianth tube, stigma apically flat, with 6 radially oriented pits on upper surface (vs. with apical part having the shape of a truncated cone and bearing numerous longitudinal grooves) and with 12 (vs. 6) dents along margin. Together with the finding described here as a separate variety, A. mirostigma is still considered endemic to Kon Plong District. Aspidistra mirostigma var. mirostigma has only been reported from its type locality, which is located 18 km from the population of A. mirostigma var. haui. Remarkably, the third currently available series of collections of A. mirostigma, the one obtained by B. Wynn-Jones at the type locality of the species (at least the specimen Wynn-Jones, BWJ 15796; photos LE: LE 01087125 https: // en. herbariumle. ru /? t = occ & id = 18649), demonstrates intermediate morphology, i. e. perianth tube with keels inside, 4 - keeled tepal lobes and stamens inserted near the base of the perianth tube as in A. mirostigma var. mirostigma, stigma with 12 dents at margin as in A. mirostigma var. haui, and low elevation at stigma apex being equally different from both varieties. The distribution pattern together with the morphological variation suggests that the two varieties are not strictly delimited from each other, and rather represent extreme variants of the gradual intraspecific diversity.
